table.name: users
table.comment: Application users with name, age, and unique email address

acceptance_criteria: AC-1  GET /api/users returns all rows ordered by id DESC (newest-first), matching legacy index.php:6.
AC-2  POST /api/users with missing or empty name returns 422 (legacy addAction.php:18-20 echoed 'Name field is empty').
AC-3  POST /api/users with missing or empty age returns 422 (legacy addAction.php:23-25).
AC-4  POST /api/users with missing or empty email returns 422 (legacy addAction.php:27-29).
AC-5  name must be 1..100 characters; out-of-range payloads return 422 (DB column varchar(100) NOT NULL).
AC-6  age must be an integer in the range 0..150; non-integer or out-of-range payloads return 422.
AC-7  email must be RFC-valid and <=100 characters; invalid format returns 422.
AC-8  POST /api/users with an email already present in the table returns 409 Conflict (new UNIQUE constraint not enforced by legacy).
AC-9  PUT /api/users/{id} that sends back the SAME email already stored on row {id} returns 200, NOT 409 (self-collision must be allowed; non-obvious requirement).
AC-10 PUT /api/users/{id} where {id} does not exist returns 404 (legacy editAction.php silently updated zero rows).
AC-11 DELETE /api/users/{id} where {id} does not exist returns 404 (legacy delete.php silently deleted zero rows then redirected).
AC-12 Path parameter {id} must coerce to a positive integer; non-integer values (e.g. 'abc') return 422 before reaching the DB.
AC-13 Destructive deletes are exposed ONLY via the HTTP DELETE verb; GET /api/users/{id} is a safe read-one and never mutates state (legacy used GET /delete.php?id=N - the new contract MUST NOT).
AC-14 POST returns 201 with the full created entity including the server-assigned id; PUT returns 200 with the updated entity; DELETE returns 204 with no body.

risk_flags.auto_resolved_by: FastAPI Path(..., gt=0) coerces id to int; non-int returns 422 before any SQL runs. SQLAlchemy uses parameter binding.
FastAPI Path(..., gt=0) coerces id to int; SQLAlchemy ORM delete uses bound parameters.
id arrives as a path int; SQLAlchemy parameter binding eliminates interpolation.
React/Next renders user data via JSX text nodes which auto-escape; the new SPA never builds HTML by string concatenation.
Unquoted attribute removed by SPA rewrite; id is carried in URL path, not a hidden form input.
React JSX auto-escapes interpolated values in the new list view.
FastAPI accepts only JSON bodies on POST/PUT; no session cookies are issued, so CSRF is structurally absent. CORS allowlist enforced at boundary.
New contract exposes delete only on HTTP DELETE; GET /api/users/{id} is a pure read. AC-13 enforces this.
